name: _test_autograd_multiple_dispatch
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI), copied verbatim from the registered schema: aten::_test_autograd_multiple_dispatch.fullcoverage(Tensor self) -> Tensor. This default call form is the one exercised bare by the original Gems pytest (flag_gems._test_autograd_multiple_dispatch(inp)); it is representative only and must not be treated as the whole operator. The original Gems pytest owns the full contract: all overloads, keyword arguments, return values, raised errors, aliasing and mutation behavior must keep passing, and no test may be removed or reference behavior adapted to fit this single signature. All supplied registered signatures, verbatim: aten::_test_autograd_multiple_dispatch.fullcoverage(Tensor self) -> Tensor; aten::_test_autograd_multiple_dispatch.fullcoverage_out(Tensor self, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!); aten::_test_autograd_multiple_dispatch.ntonly(Tensor self, bool b) -> Tensor. Per the pytest, each call form returns a fresh result tensor that matches the native ATen reference output in dtype, shape, strides and storage offset (tu.assert_result_equal plus stride and storage_offset equality), and for non-empty inputs the result's data_ptr differs from the input's. Float, fp8 (when supported), complex64, integer and bool dtype families are covered, together with 0-dim/single-element, empty and non-contiguous (sliced, transposed, stride-0 expanded) inputs, where the empty case checks only dtype, shape and strides. fullcoverage_out is the mutation/aliasing form: it writes into the caller's keyword-only out buffer and returns that same object (assert res_ret is out), matching the reference buffer's values and stride and leaving the input untouched. ntonly(self, b) carries an additional bool flag and likewise returns a fresh copy. Both backward tests check the candidate gradient against the native ATen backward run on the candidate's device; the source comments describe fullcoverage's backward as adding a constant to the incoming gradient and ntonly's as a pure copy, but the pytest asserts only equality with that native oracle. Errors such as non-tensor self, a non-bool flag and out dtype mismatch are asserted by pytest (pytest.raises) and are not expressed by this signature-level model. Kinds and defaults come from the registered schema; all parameters here are required.
